notes: Hindi (Devanagari) to Hinglish. Keys are NFC: a nukta letter (क़ ज़ फ़ ड़ …) is its consonant plus U+093C, taken before the bare consonant by the longest-key-first walk; ऩ ऱ ऴ stay single code points under NFC. Vowels are short (ा ी ू give a i u), which matches the most Dakshina romanisations; typed aa ee oo fold to the same skeleton. Anusvara and chandrabindu are n; at a word's end they are as often left unwritten (नहीं nahi, हूँ hu, में me, लोगों logo), so optionalFinals names both: such a word is also keyed by the skeleton of its walk without the n (नहीं under nhin and nhi) and either spelling spells it out, while a final न (दिन din) is always written. dropTrailing.alsoKept: a word like जगह (jagah) is jga once its h is dropped, the last a no longer between consonants; it is also keyed jgh, so a swipe that goes j, g, h without returning to a finds it (so तरह, सुबह, वजह). alsoBetweenConsonants u: the dropped vowel is often written u (hum for हम, humse, humara), so typed letters with a u between consonants are also looked up with it dropped, behind the words that have the u (कुछ, तुम, मुझे). alsoBesideConsonant e beside h: the short a before ह is said and written e (कहते kehte, रहना rehna, पहले pehle), and so is the one after that ह (बहन behen, शहर sheher), so an e between two consonants is also read as the dropped vowel when the next is h, or the one before is an h whose own vowel is dropped; typed, such a word is offered beside what the letters say as written, behind words with a real े (मेहनत, चेहरा, बेहतर), and a swipe may go by way of the e there. The words written so most are rows of chat-forms.tsv. The pairs mb/mp/mbh/mph fold to nb/np so sambhav and sanbhav meet. Medial schwa: Hindi drops the inherent vowel in V C a C V (समझना samjhna, कमरा kamra, बचपन bachpan), which the walk keeps (samajhana); dropBetweenConsonants "a" drops every a with a consonant on both sides from the skeleton, so samajhana, samajhna and samjhna meet (smjna). On the Dakshina hi test lexicon (4,502 human pairs) the typed skeleton equals the walk's 76.5% of the time with it, 60.1% without. Not expressible in format 1: (2) The final schwa is kept after a conjunct ending in र य व (मित्र mitra, कार्य karya) and in one-letter words (न na); atWordEnd.inherent drops it everywhere (mitr, n). (3) े before a word-final anusvara is typed ei (में mein, करें karein); the skeleton folds ei to e, so lookup is unaffected, only the walk's spelling. (4) Anusvara is m before प फ ब भ म (handled by the mb/mp pairs).
